bound_contract_scope: Twenty candidate-only samples exercise bound STL export, receipt-preserving import and required topology validation, then explicitly materialize plain bytes. They do not support a baseline speed comparison.
measurement_limits: Fixed baseline-then-candidate order within each pair, five sequential trials; no statistical generalization or CPU isolation claim.
Elapsed samples include counting-allocator instrumentation and correctness assertions; they are not uninstrumented production latency.
Count 16 and 128 are finite repeated workloads, not an internal total-work or heap bound.
Allocator counts exclude direct native allocations; process RSS includes runtime and library overhead.
Cold means a fresh process; warm performs 16 complete iterations before the measured work.
Geometry construction, validation, output materialization and import are included. Output destruction is recorded separately.
mutation_interpretation: Weak batch identities retain the former backing allocation after the values are dropped. Editing also allocates a new buffer. Dropping the carrier releases its witnesses; the measured allocation then disappears. Rust counters omit direct native allocations, so process RSS is reported separately.
scope: Correctness-overhead observation for a stronger evidence contract; not a same-completed-contract speedup claim.
